get.description: Returns the referral’s documents with short-lived (24h) signed download URLs. What you get depends on your side of the referral: the SENDING firm gets every document captured on the referral, plus its e-signature records; the RECEIVING firm gets only the documents the sender shared with it. No other firm may access the referral at all.

get.description: Returns a chronological, typed timeline of the client communications captured on the referral — emails, SMS, calls and notes — each entry carrying a "kind". What you get depends on your side of the referral: the SENDING firm gets the full history it captured (email bodies, call transcription and summary, notes); the RECEIVING firm gets only the communications the sender shared with it (the lead’s notes appear as a single note entry when the sender shared them). No other firm may access the referral at all.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Filter to a single activity kind. Repeat to include several.

x-webhook-events.description: A new lead was created in your account.
A referral was sent or received. Delivered to BOTH the sending and receiving firms.

Umbrella event: fires whenever a referral changes, including status changes and receiver progress (sub-status) updates. Delivered to both firms. Use the more specific referral.status_changed or referral.sub_status_changed events if you only care about one kind of change.
A referral's canonical status changed (e.g. accepted, declined, cancelled). Delivered to both firms.

The receiving firm reported progress on an accepted referral (a sub-status change such as "In contact with client" or a help request). The canonical status is unchanged. Delivered to both firms. Payload includes sub_status, previous_sub_status, sub_status_label, and an optional sub_status_note.
A referred lead was retained (signed) by the receiving firm. Delivered to both firms.
A referred case was marked settled by the receiving firm. Delivered to both firms.
